a26189db06b6: Ask: «What would you do if someone scratched your car in a parking lot?» Let the student answer however they can — then show how it sounds in Polish.
9e36370024db: Could you please send me the cost estimate?
1e766ae6c0d5: I would like to report an insurance claim.
9caaf77906bc: In your place I would take more photos.
94acc29e241b: If I had comprehensive insurance, I would repair the car myself.
a51ccc537b1a: Lesson map. In English «would» is a separate word; in Polish «by» attaches to the verb and takes a personal ending.
0ff0c2ad52f0: First the past tense without the personal ending (chciał, chciała, chcieli), then by, then the personal ending. A learner who knows the past tense already knows 90% of the form.
60307fdb40fb: The left column is men and groups that include a man, the right one is women and groups without men, just like in the past tense. Pan / pani / państwo are 3rd person, so the forms are the same as in the «on / ona» and «oni» rows.
19d26ebaa8b5: The main trap — «ó» in the masculine: mógł → mógłbym. Also here: zaczął → zacząłby, zaczęła → zaczęłaby. If the learner knows the past tense, they know these forms too.
bb1ee3783f7b: Could you call before the repair, sir?
bc7d7e865933: Could you send the invoice, madam?
878ba7add65f: Could you bring round a courtesy car?
f557cac6484f: On a phone call with an insurer or a service desk this is the most common construction. Ask the student to turn «Proszę zadzwonić» into a polite request.
3db6553c470c: Control question: can this happen, or is it an imaginary situation / too late? «Jeśli» — normal tense (present, future), «gdyby» — always with a past-tense form.
65e57dfa6449: Key idea: the personal ending attaches to «gdyby», and the verb stands in the form «wiedział / miała» without -bym. The second half of the sentence is built with -bym: Gdybym wiedział, zadzwoniłbym.
388c2d4a060d: This is not a mistake: in speech «by» with its ending can move onto a pronoun or question word. It is enough for the student to recognise these forms; let them use the neutral ones themselves.
dfd701c1ed09: Warunek to gdyby z końcówką; jakby znaczy przede wszystkim «as if».
f18c3fd1f344: In speech, Poles also say «jakbym wiedział» — the student will hear it. But in writing and on the exam — only «gdybym».
e682a5bb597a: I'd like the garage to call
918f0741237e: The second trap: English “you” has no formal/informal split, so students say «ty» (or «wy» to one person), which sounds rude or rustic to a Pole. In a service setting and at the insurer — only pan / pani.
